causalModel.founding: A vault lies under a ruined works. The party that found what had grown in the vault sealed it. The sealing party left the door welded.
causalModel.siteAdvantages: The vault is a stone undercroft with one door. The undercroft has no other opening.
causalModel.occupantsMotive: The voriplasm is sealed in the vault. The voriplasm has been sealed there for two hundred years.
causalModel.pressures: The sealing party's note is still nailed to the door. The note names what is inside the vault.
causalModel.wouldChangeIf: If the vault were opened, the voriplasm would be released. The province has a specific and unhappy history with the voriplasm.

districts.notes: A ruined Imperial court on the lake flat and a spoil berm at its east end. A hollow dug into the berm reaches the vault's front wall and its one door.

why.what: The district is the vault and the ruin court built over it.
why.whyHere: The Imperial works stood over older stone on the dry part of the lake flat. Diggers broke down to the vault's wall here.
why.whyNeighbours: The broken keep wall of the works stands west of the court, beside the track. Bramman Head lies inside the 600 m bound.
why.playerPurpose: The hollow and its door are the way into the vault. The note on the door warns what was sealed inside.
why.microGeography: The court lies on the flat at about one metre. A spoil berm about five metres high closes its east end. A hollow cut into the berm drops to a floor under two metres, at the foot of the vault's wall.

districts.notes: The broken curtain wall of the works: a fallen stub at each end, the gate across the track and a wall tower.

why.what: The district is the curtain wall of the ruined works.
why.whyHere: The penal colony walled its works where the track leaves the main track.
why.whyNeighbours: The ruin court lies inside the wall to the east. The main track passes north of the gate.
why.playerPurpose: The wall and its gate are the first things a traveller sees from the road.
why.microGeography: The wall stands on the dry lake flat at about one metre. The ground falls gently west to the track and the reeds.

parcels.orientationWhy: The wall runs north to south on the west edge of the works. The gate faces west onto the track.

why.what: The curtain wall is one run of the keep's own pieces. A fallen stub ends it at the north and a second stub ends it at the south. The gate and a wall tower stand in it.
why.whyHere: The penal colony walled its works beside the track that leaves the main track.
why.whySpot: The wall stands on the dry ground east of the shore. The track meets it at the gate.
why.whyNeighbours: The ruin court stands inside the wall. The main track passes north of it.
why.playerPurpose: A traveller on the road sees the broken wall first and walks in through the gate.
why.microGeography: The ground is firm and almost flat, a metre above the lake.

parcels.orientationWhy: The court's long side runs north to south behind the curtain wall. Its east end faces the berm.

why.what: The court is the shell of an Imperial building of the works. Broken wall lines and columns stand on its old outline. Fallen columns, loose blocks and rubble lie between them.
why.whyHere: The works stood over the vault. Its floor and roof are gone.
why.whySpot: The court fills the dry ground between the curtain wall and the berm.
why.whyNeighbours: The gate opens into its west side. The berm and the hollow lie east of it.
why.playerPurpose: The court is the ruin to explore before the vault. Its east end leads up onto the berm.
why.microGeography: The ground rises half a metre from west to east.

parcels.orientationWhy: The face runs north to south and looks west across the hollow.

why.what: The face is the vault's front wall: two lengths of Imperial fort wall, their broken ends buried in the slopes.
why.whyHere: The diggers cut down to this wall. It is the one side of the hollow that stands upright.
why.whySpot: The wall stands at the east edge of the hollow with the berm behind it.
why.whyNeighbours: The doorway is set at its foot. The stair comes down the far slope.
why.playerPurpose: The face shows where the vault begins. Its door is the only entrance.
why.microGeography: The wall's foot stands on the hollow floor; its top stands just over the berm.

parcels.orientationWhy: The doorway faces west at 270 degrees, across the hollow to the foot of the stair.

why.what: The doorway is a stone hood with its plugin's load door, set at the foot of the face. The sealing party's note is nailed on the hood.
why.whyHere: The vault has one door. The diggers reached it at the bottom of their hollow.
why.whySpot: The door stands on the hollow floor, so a visitor walks straight to it from the stair.
why.whyNeighbours: The face rises over it. Bones and a dropped tool lie on the floor in front of it.
why.playerPurpose: The door leads into the vault. The note on it warns of what was sealed inside.
why.microGeography: The hollow floor is level and dry, almost a metre above the lake.

playerPurpose.note: A hidden cache deep in the vault holds what the sealing party shut in with the voriplasm.
One authored item lies in that cache, past the boss.
The warning board over the door gives the evidence for the vault's quest.

assembly.evidence: plugin offset Skyrim.esm ImpExtDoorhole01 + ImpDoorSingleLoad01 (7 refs, e.g. 0001AB9D)

parcels.orientationWhy: The stair runs east to west down the west slope of the hollow, from the berm rim to the hollow floor.

why.what: The stair is two flights of Imperial fort steps with a short landing between them.
why.whyHere: The diggers set old steps from the works into the slope to reach the door.
why.whySpot: The stair comes down the west slope, straight across the hollow from the door.
why.whyNeighbours: Its head is on the berm at the east end of the court. Its foot faces the doorway.
why.playerPurpose: The stair leads down from the berm to the door.
why.microGeography: The west slope of the hollow drops four metres over ten metres of run.

interiorClaim.why: 1 of 9 cells plugins link to vanilla:dungeons/imperial/exterior/impextdoorhole01 pass; FortAmol01 is a dwelling, 2 exterior load doors (one entrance, paired to the lowest of 2 exterior load doors; 1 load door(s) left closed)

routes.why: The footpath goes in at the gate and turns south to the arch in the court's west wall.
A short track leaves the main road at the junction and runs south along the wall to the works gate.
The footpath crosses the ruin court from the arch to the foot of the stair up the berm.
The footpath crosses the hollow floor from the foot of the stair to the door.

approaches.sequence: From the lake flat a traveller sees the broken keep wall first. The court's columns show over it. The hollow and its door are seen last, from the berm.
approaches.wayfinding: The gate is the only way through the wall. The berm rises at the far end of the court.

approaches.sequence: From the junction the track runs south to the gate. Inside, the path crosses the court and climbs the berm. The stair goes down to the door.
approaches.wayfinding: The wall can be seen from the road. The track leaves the road at the junction.

networkTerminals.why: The place's own track meets the main track at the junction. The junction lies west of the works.

combatSpaces.why: The court and the hollow floor are open ground. The fighting happens inside the vault.

scaleGrounding.loreSource: catalogue record The Sealed Vault (voriplasm-chamber, None)
scaleGrounding.why: The vault has no occupants. The place has four built things: the curtain wall, the ruin court, the vault face and its doorway.

candidates.why: The ground is dry beside the coast-road track. Travellers on the road see the wall.
The ground is firm beside the second track. The second track climbs north-east from the lake edge.
candidates.rejectedBecause: The second track carries less traffic than the main track. The board would face fewer travellers there. No lake flat lies beside the second track for the works.
